co_fridge_with_no_name_boulder.blurb: A small cluster of boulders low in Clear Creek Canyon near Golden, tucked in the Tunnel 1 boulder zone just below the Canal Zone sub-area. It holds eleven problems, spread from easy V1 and V2 warm-ups through a handful in the V5 to V7 range, so it suits a mixed group better than a pure project session. The canyon bouldering around it picks up sun for much of the day, which makes it a popular cold-season stop. It sits only a short stroll from the car along a paved path.

_expect.name: Matt Damon on the Side of the Road Boulder

co_matt_damon_on_the_side_of_the_road_bo.blurb: A lone roadside boulder on a hillside beside Alameda Parkway, in open space near Lakewood. Eleven short problems, mostly V1 and V2 with a few up to V4, make it a quick low-commitment stop for beginners and anyone looking for a handful of easy-to-moderate pulls and a pumpy traverse. Landings are decent, but the rock still wants cleaning and some holds break, so test before trusting them and bring a pad. Rattlesnakes and coyotes are around, so watch your step in warm weather.

co_gollum_s_arch_rock.blurb: A modest granite crag on Lumpy Ridge above Estes Park, sitting just east of the big Twin Owls formation with a smaller cliff below it. Eleven mainly traditional lines run up to roughly 130 to 150 feet, from an easy 5.7 up through a cluster of 5.11 and 5.12 pitches, so it is more a place for experienced leaders than for newcomers. The namesake attraction is a sustained, left-arching crack that demands a full rack with extra large cams. Faces catch afternoon sun and it can turn hot, so cooler days suit it best. Descents are by scrambling or rappel.

co_hick_boulder.blurb: A steep, north-facing block among the pines near Maxwell Creek, in the Evergreen foothills at roughly 8,000 feet. It is the boulder nearest the Maxwell Falls hiking trail and sits directly above it. All eleven problems are hard, running from about V6 up into the V12 range, with a couple of widely repeated lines in the V7 to V10 bracket that draw strong boulderers. Expect big moves on large holds and tricky topouts. It is a poor choice for beginners.

co_crazy_diamond_boulder.blurb: A large, overhanging sandstone block in the Nine Mile bouldering zone of Unaweep Canyon, within the Dave Loves Donna group near Grand Junction. Eleven problems here lean toward the hard end: a mix of V3 and V4 lines, then several from V5 up to V8, including a few well-known harder testpieces. The stone is reported to be of very good quality. It sits roughly thirty yards south of the neighbouring Gunslinger Boulder, reached by walking south past Dave Loves Donna Boulder. Sun and shade are not well documented.
